humanities_role_explanation: Two distinct evaluations: (1) Latin-to-German/English MT on an 8-letter, 121-sentence expert-translated test set, and (2) summarization of Latin and ENH-German Bullinger letters judged against edition summaries by historians, plus a manual check of names, events and correctness. The MT task tests language-technology competence on historical-language material; the summarization with historically informed error analysis (e.g., Schweiz vs. Eidgenossenschaft, caesar as emperor) engages disciplinary content. Distinct metrics (BLEU/ChrF vs. manual 4-category scores) cover each.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Text only: 16th-century Latin and Early New High German letters translated and summarized into modern German and English.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Machine translation of Latin (and code-switched ENH-German) into modern German and English, scored by BLEU and ChrF; cross-language paragraph-wise summarization ('paraphrasing') of letters, scored by BLEU against edition summaries and by manual judgment of names, times and events, completeness and correctness.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to MT and summarization of a single 16th-century letter corpus (Latin and ENH-German); not a broad multi-task benchmark, and no benchmark is introduced.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: GPT-4 evaluated; compared against Google Translate, LingvaNex, Yandex, ModernMT, Niutrans and DeepL.

quantitative_metrics.note: BLEU, ChrF, and manual evaluation scores out of 58 paragraphs.

summary: The paper evaluates GPT-4 for machine translation of 16th-century Latin letters (Bullinger correspondence) into German and English, finding large BLEU gains over Google Translate and other online systems. It also tests GPT-4 cross-language summarization of Latin and ENH-German letters against expert-written edition summaries, with a manual evaluation showing good capture of names, events and information.
key_findings: On the 121-sentence test set GPT-4 reached BLEU 27.07 (LA-DE) and 34.50 (LA-EN) vs. Google Translate 17.53 and 25.22. Against edition summaries BLEU is low (GPT-4 MT 4.93 DE, 6.80 EN) but summaries look good: manual scores out of 58 were Names 47.2, Times & Events 54.5, Complete 48.2, Correct 43.5. No hallucinations were observed.
evaluation_unit: Latin sentence (test set of 8 letters); the summarization experiment uses 10 Latin and 10 ENH-German letters, 58 paragraphs judged manually
gold_upstream: Test set of Fischer et al. (2022): 8 letters manually translated into German by a domain expert; the English reference was machine-translated from the German with GPT-4. Summaries from the Heinrich Bullinger Briefwechsel edition (Gäbler et al. 1973-2022) written by experts of the Institute for Swiss Reformation Studies.
facets_explanation: The MT references are the Fischer et al. (2022) test set, manually translated into German by a domain expert; the English references were produced by GPT-4 (and DeepL as a check). Summarization references are the published expert-written paragraph summaries from the Bullinger edition. The paper notes completeness is sometimes subjective because editors weigh events by importance, but does not treat this as a plurality finding.
results_explanation: Best headline: GPT-4 'BLEU 34.50' for Latin into English on the 121-sentence test set (27.07 for German). The same GPT-4 translation scored 27.07 BLEU against the expert translation but only 4.93 against the human summary in German, a gap of about 22 points, derived by subtraction (27.07-4.93=22.14). No human baseline is reported; the English-German difference is attributed to resource levels, not a cultural asymmetry finding.
